verdict.summary: AMD is delivering genuine share and earnings gains across server CPUs and AI accelerators, but the equity prices a much larger future platform than current margins support. Q2 2026 revenue was $11.536 billion, up 50% year over year; Data Center revenue rose 107% to $6.718 billion and represented 58% of sales. GAAP gross and operating margins reached 54% and 17%, while non-GAAP margins were 56% and 27%. Management guided Q3 revenue to $13.0 billion plus or minus $300 million and non-GAAP gross margin to approximately 56%. The AI channel is direct through Instinct accelerators, EPYC CPUs, DPUs and rack-scale Helios systems, but AMD still depends on external foundry, packaging and HBM supply and competes with NVIDIA's software ecosystem. At 79.9x EV/EBITDA and 18.5x EV/revenue, the market assumes rapid accelerator adoption and sustained CPU share gains. $13.11 billion cash versus $4.28 billion debt is strong, though the August offering is $4.75 billion of senior debt, not equity. With no captured RTH bar, the geometry is dormant and the lifecycle remains wait.

Q2 2025 comparisons include an $800M MI308 export-control inventory charge, inflating some YoY margin improvement.

business.overview:
AMD sells Data Center processors and accelerators, Client and Gaming products, and Embedded adaptive-computing devices. Q2 Data Center revenue was $6.718B, Client/Gaming $3.8B and Embedded $977M.

The AI channel is direct: EPYC CPUs host accelerated systems, Instinct GPUs perform training and inference, DPUs/NICs move data, and Helios integrates these components at rack scale. Data Center's 58% revenue mix makes AI and server demand the dominant earnings transmission.

The model breaks if accelerator software adoption lags, foundry/HBM supply constrains ramps, export controls remove markets, or cloud customers diversify slowly. Gaming fell 31% YoY, showing that weaker legacy cycles can offset part of the data-center acceleration. Data Center now supplies the principal growth engine, but Client and Embedded cannot justify the valuation if accelerator adoption slows. The thesis breaks if hyperscalers remain CUDA-locked, MI-series gross margin trails expectations, export controls constrain shipments, or supply commitments outrun realized demand.
business.moat: AMD's moat is a portfolio and execution system: x86 CPU compatibility, chiplet design, leading-edge foundry access, acquired adaptive-computing IP and an expanding ROCm/rack-scale stack. It is a credible second-source platform, but the software moat and system control remain weaker than NVIDIA's, so performance-per-dollar must convert into deployments.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: AMD reported 1.632B shares outstanding at June 27, 2026. Q2 weighted-average shares were also 1.632B basic and 1.659B diluted after a 27M employee-equity-plan increment; the filing states excluded anti-dilutive securities were not material. The 1.659B quarterly diluted average is therefore the minimum observable denominator, while a current point-in-time theoretical fully diluted count remains unavailable. The August 14 prospectus priced $4.75B of straight senior debt across four series, and the S-3ASR created capacity only; neither changes the common denominator.

filingsReview.summary: 6 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade B measures fundamentals; trade state wait measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The Q2 Form 10-Q supports the three-segment mix and reconciles 1.632B basic weighted-average shares to 1.659B diluted shares through a 27M employee-plan increment; excluded anti-dilutive securities were not material. It also supports the manufacturing, export-control and liquidity baseline.

The August 14 final Form 424B5 prices $4.75B of straight senior debt: $1.25B 4.600% notes due 2029, $1.50B 5.000% due 2031, $1.00B 5.250% due 2033 and $1.00B 5.500% due 2036. It is not an ATM or common issuance.
The August 13 Form S-3ASR creates automatic shelf registration capacity; registration alone does not prove that AMD sold securities, received proceeds or diluted common shareholders.

The August 19 Form 8-K reports Joe Householder’s retirement, KC McClure becoming audit and finance committee chair, Nora Denzel joining that committee, and Tim Ryan’s appointment as an independent director; no securities were issued.

The FY2025 Form 10-K/A amends the audited annual filing and preserves the Data Center, Client, Gaming and Embedded segment baseline, manufacturing dependence and risk disclosures; it is not an equity or debt offering document.

The August 13 Form 424B5 is a preliminary prospectus for four senior-note series with principal amounts, coupons and maturities left blank. It is debt, not equity, and does not prove the offering had closed.
